CONFIRM C0199 | FIND: `bench/evidence.py`, `EvidenceStore.verify_bundle()`, lines in the `for i, (record, proof)` loop. The function only compares `record.get("chain_hash")` to `proof.get("chain_hash")`, then calls `self._chain.verify_inclusion_proof(proof, bundle.merkle_root)`. It never recomputes a chain hash from `record["sealed_body"]`, `record["entry_hash"]`, and `record["prev_hash"]`, and never checks `record["entry_hash"]`, `record["prev_hash"]`, or `sealed_body["payload_hash"]` against the bundled record contents. Evidence: a bundle record can be tampered by changing `sealed_body["payload"]` while leaving top-level `chain_hash` unchanged; `verify_bundle()` still accepts it because inclusion is proven only for the supplied `proof["chain_hash"]`, not for the record body. FOLLOW: this makes exported bundles misleading as “self-contained proof packages”: `EvidenceBundle.records` can contain false content while `verify_bundle()` returns success, so external audit can accept corrupted record bodies; provenance/detail consumers using bundled records are then operating on unauthenticated content.

CONFIRM C0200 | FIND: `bench/evidence.py`, `EvidenceRecord.from_chain_record()` and `_extract_finding_ids()`. Current extraction uses `_FINDING_ID_RE = re.compile(r"\bC\d{4}\b")`, so only exactly four-digit canonical IDs are indexed. Evidence from code: `from_chain_record()` populates `er.finding_ids` exclusively from `_extract_finding_ids(er.payload)` and `_extract_finding_ids(meta)`, and all finding-indexed operations depend on `self._index.by_finding`. Any valid project finding identifiers outside `Cdddd` are omitted from `query(finding_id=...)`, `trace_finding()`, `export_bundle(finding_id=...)`, and `finding_ids`. FOLLOW: omission propagates into `_classify_event()` indirectly because traces are built from `by_finding`; records that mention such IDs never enter provenance/event classification at all, so the semantic layer silently drops them rather than misclassifying them.
